name: Netlify
tagline: Web hosting platform for static sites, functions, forms, and deploy previews

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Pro listed at $20/month with credit-based usage and unlimited member changes announced in 2026.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 300 credits/month hard cap; 1 member; 1 concurrent build; 1-day observability/analytics history.
tiers.notes: All projects pause when the account exhausts its hard credit limit.

tiers.name: Personal
tiers.limits: 1,000 credits/month; 1 member; 1 concurrent build; 1 preview server; 7-day web analytics.

tiers.name: Pro 3,000 credits
tiers.limits: 3,000 credits/month; unlimited members; 3 concurrent builds; 30-day analytics; no monthly-credit rollover.

tiers.name: Pro 5,000 credits
tiers.limits: 5,000 credits/month; unlimited members; 3 concurrent builds; unused monthly credits roll for 1 additional cycle.

tiers.name: Pro 10,000 credits
tiers.limits: 10,000 credits/month; unlimited members; 3 concurrent builds; unused monthly credits roll for 1 additional cycle.

tiers.name: Pro 15,000 credits
tiers.limits: 15,000 credits/month; unlimited members; 3 concurrent builds; unused monthly credits roll for 1 additional cycle.

tiers.name: Pro 20,000 credits
tiers.limits: 20,000 credits/month; unlimited members; 3 concurrent builds; unused monthly credits roll for 1 additional cycle.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom credits, seats, builds, security, SLA and support.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 300 credits/month hard cap, 1 member, 1 concurrent build, and 1-day observability/analytics history
pricing.billingTerms: monthly only for current credit-based self-serve plans; no public annual plan
pricing.hiddenCosts: Production deploys cost 15 credits, compute 10 credits/GB-hour, bandwidth 20 credits/GB and web requests 2 credits/10,000. Pro auto-recharge is $10/1,500 credits; extra concurrent builds cost $40/month and extra preview servers $15/month. Changing a Pro credit tier deletes unused plan and rollover credits.

verdictSummary: Static hosting and functions are easy to assemble, but Netlify's value is Git-based deploys, previews, forms, redirects, edge functions, and managed platform reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Deploy static builds from git, serve via CDN/reverse proxy, add forms/functions, and create preview URLs.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because simple sites still need dependable CI/CD, routing, and previews.

priorArt.name: Coolify
priorArt.desc: Open-source self-hosted deployment platform for apps, databases, and static sites.

alternatives.name: Netlify Free
alternatives.desc: The same service covers a small production site indefinitely: Git deploys, previews, functions, forms, TLS, and 300 monthly credits.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Cloudflare Pages Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Previews and functions are excellent; the missing built-in forms service means it does not replace the whole Netlify job.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Coolify
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Great for hosting apps, but deploy previews, serverless functions, and a managed form inbox do not arrive as one finished product.

notes: Good to pair with Vercel; users can compare platform lock-in vs self-hosting.
prompt:
Build me a personal static-site deploy pipeline to replace Netlify, running on my own
VPS. Requirements:

- A small deploy service: Node + Express receiving a GitHub webhook on localhost, with
  Caddy in front serving the built sites over HTTPS.
- On push to main: pull the repo into /srv/sites/<repo>/, run the build command from a
  per-site config (sites.json: repo, branch, buildCmd, outputDir), and atomically swap a
  `current` symlink to the new build.
- Keep the last 5 builds per site on disk so rollback is `deployctl rollback <site>`, a
  one-line CLI.
- Branch previews: pushes to other branches deploy to <branch>.<site>.mydomain.com via a
  Caddy wildcard route.
- Build logs go to /srv/sites/<repo>/logs/<timestamp>.log; `deployctl status` lists
  sites, last deploy time, and pass/fail.
- Webhook secret and tokens in .env. The service binds to localhost behind Caddy; no
  accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: CDN/edge functions, form handling, and team features. This is one VPS,
  not a global network. Skip the dashboard UI, the CLI is enough.
- README: the Caddy config snippet, GitHub webhook setup, and the wildcard DNS record
  previews need.
